## Setup

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

The hooks in `.githooks/` run the `just` recipes below. `uv run` under `python/` creates
the environment on first use, with `beliefs` as an editable path dependency.

## Gates

- Tests: `just test-one <pytest args>` runs the test at hand: a path relative to `python/`,
  `tests/test_file.py::test_name`, or `-k "a and b"`; at least one argument is required.
  `just test-fast` is the inner loop (pytest-testmon selects affected tests from its
  dependency data); run it before committing. `just test` runs the suite.
  All test recipes run under ops' `host-budget run`, which sizes
  `-n auto` to the host's budget. `just check` runs the seconds-long gate;
  `just gate` runs both. All test recipes run in a worktree as they are. Every recipe
  records its run through `tools/tt`, the timing wrapper vendored from the ops
  repository; do not call `pytest` directly.
- The pre-commit hook classifies every staged path against `docs_paths` in the justfile:
  only `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/*.md` and `tasks/*.md` take `hook-pre-commit-docs`.
  Markdown command fixtures are excluded; renames count on both sides and failed
  classification runs the full check. Both checks currently run ops-check, ops-docs check and tasks check.
- There is no CI workflow, so `ci_suite_refs` is empty and the pre-push hook always
  carries the full suite through `just hook-pre-push`. `hook-pre-push-fast` is available
  for future CI-covered push refs and uses testmon's dependency selection. Run `just test`
  yourself only when hooks are not installed, the fast target does not cover the affected
  behavior, or you are asked to.

## Layout

- `commands/<name>/` — `command.toml` and `prompt.md` per command; `tools/cli.toml` is
  the authority for the surface.
- `python/` — the package; tests under `python/tests/`.

## Rules

- Every scientific record is a governed record in a `beliefs` corpus, written as a kernel
  act through the permit-bound writer endpoint; science keeps no record storage of its
  own. Two write classes leave evidence in the `beliefs` session ledger instead of a
  corpus: `session` (`project-select`'s selection line) and `sharing` (`provider-bind`
  and `adopt`'s sharing lines). The sharing registry under `sharing_root`
  (`science.sharing`) is science-owned state: its pins and provider bindings
  are a projection of those lines, written only by sharing commands after the line
  each projects and rebuildable from the ledger by `replay`; the adopted corpora beside
  them are `beliefs` corpora the kernel restores. The second science-owned state is
  presentation only: historical sharing-report tails under
  `operations_root/tails/<session_id>/<invocation_id>.json`. The dispatcher rebuilds
  every pin block from the ledger and appends this informational sidecar, never
  kernel evidence, a close outcome, or a recomputable cache. An absent sidecar means
  an empty tail; losing a nonempty tail loses commentary and stales its cursor while
  every effect remains recoverable. Milestone 1b plan review round 5 accepted this
  narrow exception; its cost is retaining the sidecar beside the ledger for exact
  historical replay (framework design §4.4, §6.1, §7.3–§7.4).
- A new command is a row in `tools/cli.toml` first; the conformance test asserts the
  live parser surface equals it.
